description:
Somos un equipo formado por tres chicas con muchas ganas de participar, aprender y vivir esta experiencia. Nos interesa mucho todo lo relacionado con la tecnología, el espacio, la exploración espacial y la creatividad.

Nos gusta aprender cosas nuevas, compartir ideas, trabajar en equipo y animarnos a nuevos desafíos. Tenemos muchas ganas de aportar nuestras habilidades, desarrollar proyectos y dar lo mejor de nosotras.

También estamos abiertas a que se sumen más personas al equipo.
summary: This is a technological innovation project focused on developing an autonomous system for future scientific expeditions to Mars. The proposal involves designing modular stations capable of monitoring and helping to mitigate radiation exposure, investigating the conversion of various types of radiation into electrical energy, and storing the electricity generated. Furthermore, it incorporates stabilization systems and the reuse of materials from decommissioned solar panels, promoting resource utilization and sustainability in space exploration.
details:
RAIDER is a scientific and technological project designed to investigate the environmental conditions of Mars and develop alternatives for making use of the planet's available resources. It consists of a network of autonomous stations that could be distributed across the Martian surface to study different types of radiation, generate and store electrical energy, and evaluate anchoring systems adapted to the characteristics of the Martian soil.

 The system includes three specialized modules. The first is designed to capture solar radiation through photovoltaic cells, converting sunlight into electrical energy. The second focuses on ultraviolet radiation, which is part of the solar spectrum, and uses specific semiconductor materials to study its detection and potential energy conversion. The third module is designed to detect and analyze galactic cosmic rays, high-energy particles that come from outer space. It uses sensors and materials capable of registering their interactions and producing electrical signals that can be analyzed for scientific purposes. The electricity generated mainly by the solar modules would be regulated and stored in batteries so it could be used when needed.

 RAIDER also incorporates a stabilization and anchoring system that combines magnetic elements with mechanical fasteners. Its design takes into account the presence of magnetic minerals in Martian soil, such as magnetite and maghemite, which could interact with magnets placed in the station's base. This magnetic interaction would be complemented by mechanical anchors to improve stability and prevent unwanted movement. The overall structure has a modular design inspired by the shape of a flower, with different sections performing specific functions.

 One of the project's main benefits is its potential to provide information about radiation on Mars and contribute to the development of more autonomous technologies for future space missions. It also aims to investigate new ways of generating and storing energy, reducing dependence on external supplies. Furthermore, RAIDER proposes reusing materials from decommissioned solar panels, such as aluminum, copper, glass, and electrical components that can still be safely used. In this way, it incorporates the principles of a circular economy and seeks to reduce material waste.

 RAIDER's creativity lies in bringing different technologies together in a single system. It combines radiation research, photovoltaic energy conversion, energy storage, particle detection, and magnetic and mechanical stabilization. Another innovative aspect is the use of Mars' geological characteristics and recycled materials as part of the design, rather than relying exclusively on newly manufactured components.

 During the development of the project, the team considered several environmental conditions on Mars, including its atmosphere, radiation levels, temperature variations, dust, sunlight availability, soil properties, and low gravity. The team also considered material resistance, energy consumption, operational autonomy, maintenance, and the possibility of recovering and reusing components. The proposed technologies include photovoltaic cells, sensors, magnets, batteries, electronic circuits, and control systems. In a future implementation, these systems could be monitored using microcontrollers and data-processing software.

In addition, we have developed a map that traces the path of a past NASA mission—the "Curiosity" rover—while highlighting the locations of the minerals used in our project and explaining their functions.
This map features a 3D overview and offers a first-person perspective, allowing you to walk, run, jump, and examine the minerals.

 The expected impact of RAIDER is to contribute to scientific knowledge about Mars and the development of technologies that could support future exploration. Its implementation could provide valuable environmental data, improve mission planning, and introduce new possibilities for energy use and material recycling. Although the project is still a proposal and some of its applications require further research and experimental testing, its purpose is to demonstrate how the integration of different scientific and technological fields can help address the challenges of space exploration.

 Ultimately, RAIDER aims to develop an autonomous system capable of studying the Martian environment, exploring new energy possibilities, and adapting to the conditions of a planet different from our own, combining innovation, sustainability, and scientific research.
